item: The data files are checked table by table after an unexpected stop, before collection writes again (E2)
key_paths: src/database/verify.py; src/database/damage.py; src/scheduler/storage_guard.py; src/scheduler/runner.py; src/wiki/runner.py; src/api/boot_sequence.py; src/api/main.py; src/static/app-core.js; src/static/taskmanager.js; tests/test_database_verify.py; tests/test_boot_sequence.py; tests/storage_guard_node_test.js; src/backup/merge.py
summary: After a session that did not end cleanly (the ledger's clean is False; an unknown end is not a reason) or a check left unfinished (at most 3 starts in a row), the corpus, Wikipedia and law files are read once each, table by table (smallest first by the planner's statistics) with PRAGMA quick_check(table) on its own read-only connection through the one connect() factory, armed in the start-up upkeep before the boot-sequence thread exists and run as its first step. From arming to the end, admit() answers verifying (phase paused-verifying), the Wikipedia lane and off-peak maintenance wait, Resume anyway is refused with its own sentence and the task manager and vitals panel show table N of M; the check always ends (a finally, a disarm when the thread cannot start) and is read once per process. A table is damaged only on a non-ok answer or SQLITE_CORRUPT; busy, locked, I/O error, interrupt, missing file, wrong or missing passphrase and a stop are unchecked with the reason, never damage, and a stopped run leaves the entry running so the next start reads again. A damaged table latches its file through the same _apply_incident a corruption error uses (search-index scope only when every damaged table is the index's). database-damage.json gains a per-file verification block (verdict and seconds per table, page facts, trigger, attempts), carried by the diagnostics member (cut to the verdicts when small). The check is armed as the start-up upkeep's first statement, before its slow steps, and the wait is ended in a finally unless the thread that runs the check was started; a due check is recorded as owed (also by a boot that stays locked), so a session closed before it began does not cancel it, and owing is not an attempt; a damaged verdict survives a restart (the file is read again at every start until it reads clean or is replaced), and an error FTS5 reports as a row (out of memory, I/O, full) is unchecked, never damage. Four new strings x12 and the damage hover reworded x12. Each claim has a test on real damaged copies (plaintext, SQLCipher, FTS5), and the main ones were run against a mutant of their code. Not built: repair and salvage (E3), an operator skip.
